characters.name: Gabriel John Utterson
characters.description: A sober, respectable London lawyer; friend and trustee to Dr. Jekyll and central investigator of the Hyde mystery.

characters.name: Edward Hyde
characters.description: A small, violent, repulsive man who is the beneficiary in Dr. Jekyll’s will and the agent of brutal acts; later revealed as Jekyll’s alter ego.

characters.name: Henry Jekyll
characters.description: Prominent physician and scientist who composes a drug enabling transformation into Hyde; author of the final confession.

characters.name: Richard Enfield
characters.description: Utterson’s distant kinsman and man-about-town who tells the opening "story of the door" about Hyde trampling a child.

characters.name: Hastie Lanyon
characters.description: A hearty, formerly close friend of Jekyll and Utterson and a physician who witnesses the Jekyll/Hyde transformation; dies of shock.

characters.name: Poole
characters.description: Long-serving servant and butler to Dr. Jekyll who raises the alarm about strange occurrences in the laboratory and leads Utterson to force the cabinet door.

characters.name: Mr. Guest
characters.description: Utterson’s head clerk; a handwriting student who compares Jekyll’s note and Hyde’s letter and notices their similarity.

characters.name: Sir Danvers Carew
characters.description: An elderly, highly respected gentleman and Member of Parliament who is brutally murdered in the street.

characters.name: Inspector Newcomen
characters.description: Police inspector of Scotland Yard who investigates Hyde’s rooms after the Carew murder.

characters.name: a maid servant (Carew murder witness)
characters.description: A maid living alone who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew from her window and summons the police.

characters.name: a girl of maybe eight or ten
characters.description: The child trampled by Hyde in Enfield’s account; member of the family who confronts the man.

characters.name: the child’s family
characters.description: The girl’s relatives who turn out at the scene and confront the man who trampled the child.

characters.name: the apothecary (Sawbones)
characters.description: The cut-and-dry apothecary/doctor in Enfield’s tale (not named) who, like others, reacts violently to Hyde’s presence; referred to as ‘Sawbones.’

characters.name: the old woman (Hyde’s housekeeper)
characters.description: An ivory-faced, silvery-haired elderly woman who answers the door at Hyde’s Soho rooms and acts as his housekeeper.

characters.name: the housemaid (Jekyll’s)
characters.description: A housemaid in Jekyll’s household who reacts hysterically on being told of the situation during Poole’s alarm.

characters.name: the knife-boy
characters.description: A young kitchen servant present among Jekyll’s household when Poole and Utterson arrive; tasked during the planned watch.

characters.name: Bradshaw
characters.description: A footman in Jekyll’s service who is given instructions by Utterson to post at the laboratory door during the forced entry.

characters.name: the locksmith
characters.description: The locksmith called (with a carpenter) to force Jekyll’s cabinet/old theatre door as instructed in Lanyon’s letter.

characters.name: the carpenter
characters.description: The carpenter summoned with the locksmith to force the strong door of the cabinet/theatre.

characters.name: a policeman
characters.description: An unnamed beat policeman referenced in Lanyon’s narrative; noticed near the scene as the midnight visitor approaches.

characters.name: the hansom driver / driver
characters.description: A cab/hansom driver encountered by Hyde (Jekyll/Hyde) during his movements in the city; the driver reacts to Hyde’s appearance.
